scope: Functional McKernel OS/apps and Rust/assembly migration only; no security testing.
findings: Existing Rust returns an unheld thread after releasing threads_lock, then calls hold_thread; C retains inside the lock. The successor acquires a positive non-overflowing thread ref under threads reader and transfers exactly one ref to existing cleanup. It requires the hash-independent sibling-lock lifetime guarantee and no force-refcount reset.

Exact live task returns held thread; unavailable task exits with no held thread or process/VM refs, unlocks the process, and nulls borrowed proc before cleanup. Non-task lookup may retain first viable other thread; absent viable thread now continues process/VM-only entries. STATUS and STAT guard the missing thread before dereference and finish the normal error path.

Successor1 guarded all entries on missing fallback, causing an observable regression to process-only entries. Successor2 corrects this. Baseline C `thread == NULL` after intrusive-list iteration cannot establish intended absent-list behavior because container-of sentinel is not necessarily NULL.
A comment replacing the removed extern preserves all four preceding allocation/free line! origin lines 153,159,164,169.

Separate unresolved paths include Process 0-to-1 resurrection by find_process plus hold_process and VM lifetime while acquiring its reference, direct do_kill acquisitions, and force-to-one refcount reset. This review does not declare procfs or general lifecycle acceptance.
fixture_scope: Author reports lookup and caller-slice unit fixtures passed individually 1/1 after rustc 1.85.1 correction; actual extracted candidate bodies with mocked layouts, lock, and callbacks. Lookup fixture does not run real concurrency; caller fixture is sliced, not a full procfs request. Reviewer inspected sources and did not rerun tests. Actual header/layout, true MCS/IRQ, integrated compile and native checks remain open.
